transfer_rules.residency_condition: Applies to residents (居住者) under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act who make or receive the payment
transfer_rules.rule_name: Report of payments/receipts above JPY 30 million
transfer_rules.rule_summary: If a Japan resident sends money abroad or receives money from abroad in an amount above the equivalent of JPY 30 million, a payment report must be filed with the Minister of Finance through the Bank of Japan. Payments of JPY 30 million or less are exempt.
documents_required: 支払又は支払の受領に関する報告書 (Report on Payments or Receipt of Payments)
transfer_rules.restrictions: Paper report for a payment made through a bank: file within 10 days of the payment, via the bank or fund-transfer provider that handled it. Online filing: within 20 days, directly to the Bank of Japan.
transfer_rules.exceptions: Payments/receipts of JPY 30 million equivalent or less (3千万円相当額以下) are exempt. The amount is converted to yen at the rate set out on the BOJ page.
transfer_rules.regulator: Ministry of Finance Japan (reports submitted via the Bank of Japan)
transfer_rules.evidence_quote: 日本銀行を経由して財務大臣に提出する

transfer_rules.rule_name: Bank legality/sanctions check on overseas remittances (適法性の確認)
transfer_rules.rule_summary: Before handling an overseas transfer you send or receive, Japanese banks must check under the Foreign Exchange Act that it is not caught by sanctions or other controls. The bank may ask about the sender, the recipient, the purpose and supporting documents.
transfer_rules.restrictions: The bank cannot process a payment until it has confirmed that the payment is not subject to FEFTA controls, or that a permit has been obtained.
transfer_rules.evidence_quote: 外為法に基づき確認することが求められています

transfer_rules.rule_name: Asset-freeze sanctions: payments to designated persons need a permit
transfer_rules.rule_summary: Payments to people or entities designated under Japan's economic sanctions require government permission, so in practice they are blocked. Banks screen customers against sanctions lists before opening accounts and before handling transfers.
transfer_rules.restrictions: Payments to persons designated by Ministry of Foreign Affairs notice are placed under a permission system (example page: measures relating to the situation in Ukraine). Under MOF inspection guidelines, banks must confirm before starting a deposit relationship that the customer and its beneficial owner are not sanctioned persons.
transfer_rules.exceptions: Allowed only with a permit from the Minister of Finance.
transfer_rules.evidence_quote: 外務省告示により指定された者に対する支払等を許可制とする。

transfer_rules.rule_name: Customs declaration for cash/means of payment above JPY 1 million
transfer_rules.rule_summary: If you enter or leave Japan carrying cash, cheques (including traveller's cheques), promissory notes or securities worth more than JPY 1 million in total, in any currency, you must declare them to Customs.
documents_required: Declaration of Carrying of Means of Payment (paper form at airport/seaport Customs, or online via NACCS)
transfer_rules.restrictions: Gold of over 90% purity weighing more than 1 kg in total must also be declared.
transfer_rules.exceptions: The threshold is JPY 100,000 (10万円) for travellers bound for North Korea.

transfer_rules.rule_name: My Number required for overseas remittances
transfer_rules.rule_summary: Japanese law requires you to give your bank your Individual Number (My Number) before you can send money abroad or receive it from abroad. Banks may also ask about the purpose of the transaction.
transfer_rules.restrictions: MUFG, SMBC, Mizuho and Japan Post Bank all state that My Number registration is needed for overseas transfers. Japan Post Bank's service works only from accounts that have completed identity verification (取引時確認) and My Number registration.
transfer_rules.evidence_quote: 法令により外国送金のお取引の際は、個人番号（マイナンバー）

transfer_rules.rule_name: Identity verification for overseas transfers (本人確認)
transfer_rules.rule_summary: Banks verify your identity for overseas transfers under the Act on Prevention of Transfer of Criminal Proceeds and the Foreign Exchange Act. Your ID must be valid on the day you present it.
documents_required: Valid photo ID such as the residence card (在留カード)
transfer_rules.restrictions: SMBC states that banks may need to confirm more than the law requires, depending on the nature and circumstances of the transaction.
transfer_rules.evidence_quote: 法令（犯罪収益移転防止法・外為法等）の定めに基づきお客さまご本人の確認

transfer_rules.rule_name: Tuition invoice as proof of remittance purpose
transfer_rules.rule_summary: When you send tuition abroad, the bank may ask for a document showing the purpose, such as the school's tuition invoice.
documents_required: Tuition invoice or similar document showing the purpose (送金目的を確認できる資料)
transfer_rules.evidence_quote: 送金目的を確認できる資料：留学費用（授業料）の請求書等

transfer_rules.residency_condition: Non-resident by default; treated as a resident once 6+ months have passed since entering Japan, or if working at an office in Japan
transfer_rules.rule_summary: Under the foreign-exchange rules, a foreign national is treated as a non-resident until 6 months after entering Japan, unless they work at an office in Japan. A newly arrived student may therefore face some limits on banking services at first.
transfer_rules.restrictions: MUFG states that non-residents are subject to some restrictions on banking services. Mizuho states that non-residents cannot hold a consolidated account (総合口座).
transfer_rules.exceptions: Treated as non-residents in all cases: people on official duty for a foreign government or international organisation, and diplomats or consular officers.
transfer_rules.evidence_quote: 本邦に入国後６月以上経過するに至つた者

transfer_rules.rule_name: Japan Post Bank international remittance limits
transfer_rules.rule_summary: Japan Post Bank's online international transfer service only accepts transfers under JPY 1 million each, up to JPY 2 million a day and JPY 5 million a month. These are the bank's own limits, not a national law.
documents_required: Account with completed identity verification (取引時確認)
transfer_rules.restrictions: Each transfer must be under JPY 1,000,000 (100万円未満); daily total JPY 2,000,000 or less; monthly total JPY 5,000,000 or less, converted at the rate applied when you apply. Individuals only. The bank may refuse an application after review.
transfer_rules.regulator: Japan Post Bank Co., Ltd. (bank product limit)
transfer_rules.evidence_quote: 1回あたり100万円未満、1日あたり200万円以下、1か月あたり500万円以下

transfer_rules.rule_name: Selling or handing over your bank account is a crime
transfer_rules.rule_summary: Selling or handing over your passbook or cash card so that someone else can use your account is a crime in Japan. This includes when you leave Japan: close the account instead.
transfer_rules.restrictions: Japan Post Bank asks customers moving out of Japan, for example when returning home, to close their account.
transfer_rules.regulator: Japan Post Bank Co., Ltd. (bank guidance; the statute is not named on the page)
transfer_rules.evidence_quote: 口座(通帳・キャッシュカード)の譲渡や売買は犯罪です

transfer_rules.nationality_condition: Foreign nationals holding a residence card
transfer_rules.visa_condition: Any status of residence with a period of stay, including Student (留学)
transfer_rules.rule_name: Report residence-card renewals; close the account when you leave
transfer_rules.rule_summary: Banks record your period of stay. If it expires and you do not send them your renewed residence card, they may restrict your account. When you leave Japan for good, close the account.
documents_required: Copy of the renewed residence card (在留カード)
transfer_rules.restrictions: MUFG may restrict transactions under its deposit rules if the customer does not respond by the deadline. Japan Post Bank and Mizuho state similar restrictions.
transfer_rules.evidence_quote: 口座をご利用されなくなった場合には、口座のご解約をお願いいたします

account_opening.summary: International students holding a residence card (在留カード) can open an ordinary account at the major Japanese banks. Banks check the period of stay on the card: Mizuho and Japan Post Bank refuse applications if fewer than 3 months of stay remain, and Japan Post Bank will not open accounts for people whose original period of stay was 3 months or less and who have no residence card. Under the foreign-exchange rules a foreign national counts as a non-resident until 6 months after entering Japan (unless working at an office in Japan), and MUFG says non-residents face some restrictions on banking services. Foreign nationals cannot use MUFG's online 'Smart' account opening and must be verified at a branch. Register your address at the municipal office within 14 days of moving in, because Japan Post Bank cannot open an account if the residence card shows no address. Tell the bank when your address or period of stay changes, and close the account when you leave Japan.
typical_documents: Residence card (在留カード), showing your current address (Japan Post Bank does not accept a card without an address; its app does not accept a card without a photo)
Student ID or certificate of enrollment (Mizuho; Japan Post Bank for 留学 status holders)
Personal seal or signature (no rubber Shachihata-type stamps)
Document confirming your Individual Number (My Number): required by MUFG at account opening, and by all four banks for overseas remittances
Passport or residence certificate (住民票) may also be requested, for example for residence cards issued on or after 14 June 2026 (MUFG) or newer-format cards (Mizuho)
Mobile phone number: the Japan Post Bank app uses it for identity verification by voice call or SMS
eligibility_factors: Remaining period of stay: Mizuho and Japan Post Bank refuse applications if your stay ends within 3 months

FEFTA residency: non-resident for the first 6 months after entry unless working at an office in Japan; MUFG says non-residents face some service restrictions and Mizuho does not allow them a consolidated account (総合口座)
Address registered on the residence card (moving-in notification at the municipal office within 14 days, per the Immigration Services Agency guidebook)
Age: Japan Post Bank accepts applications from account holders aged 16 or over (younger children through a parent); MUFG requires a parent's application for under-15s
Branch visit: MUFG requires foreign nationals and dual nationals to be verified at a branch (they cannot use Smart account opening)
AML questioning: banks confirm customer information and purpose of the account or transaction

banks.visa_requirements: Residence card required; MUFG checks the period and status of residence on it. Customers who have lived in Japan for more than 6 months are treated as residents; non-residents are subject to some restrictions on banking services.
documents: Passport or residence certificate (住民票) may be requested for residence cards issued on or after 14 June 2026
banks.monthly_fee: No monthly fee found. Paper passbook: JPY 550 a year (tax incl.) for ordinary accounts opened on or after 1 April 2022 (not charged to customers under 18 or 70 and over at the end of January). Unused-account fee: JPY 1,320 a year (tax incl.) may apply to accounts opened on or after 1 July 2021 and unused for 2+ years.
banks.credit_card_available: Group card company Mitsubishi UFJ NICOS offers student cards (for university, graduate, junior college and vocational students) and accepts a residence card as ID. Its page does not state foreign-national eligibility, and screening criteria are not disclosed.
banks.evidence_quote: resided in Japan for longer than six months (Residents)
banks.notes: Foreign and dual nationals must be verified at a branch; they cannot use 'Smart account opening'. Applicants under 15 need a parent to apply. Overseas transfers are available via Mitsubishi UFJ Direct (online) and at branch counters; My Number is required by law, and the bank may ask the purpose. A pre-expiry notice asks customers to send a copy of the renewed residence card, otherwise transactions may be restricted, and to close the account when leaving Japan. No dedicated student account was found.

banks.account_type: Ordinary deposit account (普通預金), opened as an 'Olive' account via smartphone
banks.visa_requirements: Foreign nationals must provide a residence card or special permanent resident certificate. No residence-period requirement was stated on the fetched page.
documents: Residence card (在留カード) or special permanent resident certificate (特別永住者証明書)
banks.monthly_fee: Olive: no annual fee (年会費無料); ATM fees are waived when conditions are met.
banks.credit_card_available: Group company Sumitomo Mitsui Card's general guidance says foreigners who meet conditions (a residence card, which requires a stay of 3+ months) can generally get a Japanese credit card, subject to screening of attributes and credit information. The article states it does not describe Sumitomo Mitsui Card's actual screening criteria.
banks.evidence_quote: 外国籍の方は在留カードもしくは特別永住者証明書の内、いずれか1点をご用意ください
banks.notes: SMBC says high school and university students can open an account themselves. Applicants under 15 cannot use selfie verification (a parent applies). Overseas transfers run 24 hours via SMBC Direct after applying for the service; My Number notification is required. Not available via telephone banking.

banks.account_type: Ordinary deposit account (Mizuho e-Account; no bankbook issued automatically)
banks.visa_requirements: Residence card (including Specified Residence Card) required. Applications are refused if your period of stay ends in less than 3 months. Non-residents cannot hold consolidated accounts (総合口座).
documents: Student ID or certificate of enrollment (or employee ID)
Personal seal or signature (no Shachihata-type rubber seals)
Passport may also be requested for newer residence cards
banks.evidence_quote: If your period of stay will end in less than three months
banks.notes: Online and branch account opening are available in Japanese only. For AML purposes the bank checks residence expiry, work restrictions and residence card number. Overseas transfers are for Mizuho account holders at selected branches (some by video call with a booking), and not via the Internet branch. My Number is required. A tuition invoice is accepted as proof of purpose. Incoming overseas transfers cost JPY 2,500 each for individuals. Inform Mizuho when your stay is extended, and close the account when you leave Japan.

banks.visa_requirements: Residence card required (with current address; extra documents if the card has no photo). Applications are refused if the period of stay expires within 3 months of applying. People whose original period of stay was 3 months or less and who have no residence card cannot open an account. 留学 (Student) status holders must also show a student ID.
documents: Residence card (在留カード) showing current address
Student ID (for 留学 / Student status)
Additional ID such as residence certificate (住民票の写し) if the card has no photo
Phone number (the app uses voice call or SMS verification)
banks.monthly_fee: No account fee found. ATM fees apply to deposits or withdrawals with coins. Deposit cap of JPY 13 million per person each for ordinary and time savings.
banks.evidence_quote: ３か月以内に到来する場合、口座開設はいたしかねます
banks.notes: Minimum age 16 applies to applicants applying for themselves; accounts for children aged 15 or under are opened by a parent. Counter and Yucho Direct international remittances ended 29 and 31 August 2025, replaced by the online 'ゆうちょの国際送金' service, launched in July 2025, for individuals with My Number registered and identity verification completed. Limits: under JPY 1M per transfer, JPY 2M a day, JPY 5M a month. Update your residence card and address after renewals or moves, or transactions may be temporarily restricted. Close the account when leaving Japan.

bureaus: Personal Credit Information Center (全国銀行個人信用情報センター, often called KSC): set up and run by the Japanese Bankers Association; members are mainly banks and government-affiliated lenders
CIC (株式会社シー・アイ・シー / Credit Information Center Corp.): members are mainly credit card and installment-sales companies
JICC (株式会社日本信用情報機構 / Japan Credit Information Reference Center Corp.): members are mainly consumer finance companies
what_contributes: Identity information: name, date of birth, sex, address, phone number, employer
Contract details and repayment history for loans and credit cards, including whether payments were made, late payments, subrogated repayment and enforced collection
Inquiry records: date a member checked your file and details of the loan or card applied for; shared with members for up to 6 months, disclosed to you for up to 1 year
Bankruptcy or civil rehabilitation decisions published in the official gazette (kept up to 7 years at KSC)
Contract information is kept during the contract and up to 5 years after it ends (or after full repayment)
why_it_matters: Banks and credit companies share credit information through the bureaus and use it to decide whether to approve loans and cards
Late-payment and similar adverse information is exchanged among all three bureaus, so a missed payment with one company can affect applications elsewhere
Members use the KSC to prevent over-lending (multiple debts) and to speed up screening
responsible_behaviours: Pay every card, loan and installment bill on time, including smartphone handset installments
Request disclosure (開示請求) from each bureau to check how your information is registered
Keep the number of new credit applications low: each one leaves an inquiry record that members can see for up to 6 months
risks: Late payment of smartphone handset installments is registered with credit bureaus such as CIC, JICC and KSC, and can count against later card or loan applications
Adverse information is shared across all three bureaus
Contract and repayment records remain for up to 5 years after the contract ends; gazetted bankruptcy information for up to 7 years at KSC
credit_system.foreigner_notes: Sumitomo Mitsui Card's general guidance says foreign residents can usually get a Japanese credit card if they hold a residence card or special permanent resident certificate, which requires a stay of 3+ months; people staying under 3 months cannot get one even with a passport and visa. Screening mainly looks at the applicant's attributes and credit information. Issuers do not publish their actual screening criteria. No official page confirming how foreign (overseas) credit history is treated was found.
